title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). 𝔖^+ is a discrete model of SL(2,Z), generated by ρ of order 6 and σ of order 4 with ρ^3 = σ^2 = -1. 𝔊 = 𝔖^+·{1,τ} is a GL(2,Z)-type extension by an orientation-reversing involution τ. Π ≅ Γ(2) is the fundamental group of M_{0,3} (the λ-line) extended by μ = {±1} = centre. Π_0 ⊂ Π is a torsion-free complement of μ. It is free on λ_0, λ_1, and the previous page suggests λ_i = -l_i with l_i the unipotent loops, so that λ_0 λ_1 λ_∞ = 1 and Π_0 is stable under ρ. The previous page showed that the profinite Π_0^ is normalised by the automorphism group M (Grothendieck–Teichmüller type) acting on the profinite 𝔖^+. Hence Π^ = Π_0^ × μ (22).

This page does the bookkeeping for the orientation-reversing part.
- (23) Two Klein four-groups: D_τ = {1,τ} × μ and D_σ = {1,σ} × μ.
- (24) Their intersections with Π are μ, and with Π_0 they are trivial. The same holds after profinite completion.
- (25)–(26) Enlarged groups Π_τ = μ_τ·Π = D_τ·Π_0 and Π_{0,τ} = μ_τ·Π_0, with splittings Π_τ = Π_{0,τ} × μ (similarly for σ).
- (27) Normalisation of the cocycle data. The formulas (20) for u in M, namely u(ρ) = int(α)ρ and u(σ) = ε_2 int(β)σ, fix α, β only modulo the centre μ. One removes this ambiguity by requiring α ∈ Π_{0,τ}^ and β ∈ Π_0^. This is analogous to the normalisation of Drinfeld/Ihara parameters (e.g. f in the commutator subgroup).
- (28) Presentation of the finite quotient 𝔊/Π_0, of order 24. It has generators ρ, σ, τ with ρ^6 = σ^4 = τ^2 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, τστ^{-1} = σ^{-1}, and a relation between τ and ρ. The relation τρτ^{-1} = ρ^{-1} is crossed out and replaced by τ(ρ) = ρ. The justification is (29): τ(ρ) = (-λ_1^{-1})ρ in 𝔊, reduced modulo Π_0, with the remark that λ_∞ = λ_0 = 1 follows by conjugating by ρ.
- On the next page he changes generator to τ' (in effect τ' = τσ). This gives the more symmetric presentation τ'ρτ'^{-1} = ρ^{-1}, τ'στ'^{-1} = σ^{-1}, σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}. The subgroup 𝔖^+/Π_0 is then the dicyclic (binary dihedral) group of order 12, a central extension of S_3 by ±1.

Purpose: an explicit finite-level model of how the Teichmüller-type automorphism group M of SL2(Z)^ (and its GL2 extension) acts. The next page computes that the automorphisms of the extension 1→μ→𝔖^+/Π_0→S_3→1 inducing the identity on S_3 form Z/2, generated by x ↦ sg(x)x.
errors: (24) 'D_τ ∩ 𝔊 = μ' cannot be meant literally, since D_τ ⊂ 𝔊. Presumably the intended group is the orientation-preserving 𝔖^+ (∩ 𝔖^+ = μ), or the first equality is a slip.

Sign issue in (28)/(29). If λ_1 ∈ Π_0 and '-' denotes the central element -1, then reducing (29) modulo Π_0 gives τρτ^{-1} ≡ -ρ = ρ^4, not ρ. The statement '-λ_1^{-1} = 1 i.e. λ_1 = 1' is then inconsistent as written. Either λ_1 here means the unipotent l_1 (with λ_1 = -l_1 only on the previous page), or the third relation of (28) depends on which complement Π_0 of μ in Π was chosen. A check in GL2(Z): with τ = [[0,1],[1,0]] one gets τρτ = ρ^{-1} exactly; with τ = diag(1,-1) one gets τρτ = -l·ρ^{-1}. So the correct relation hinges on these conventions. Grothendieck's switch to τ' on the next page suggests he was himself adjusting this.
The phrase 'modulo μ' in the normalisation paragraph is a reading of an unclear word. Note also that α lives in Π^·{1,τ}, so the normalisation α ∈ Π_{0,τ} rather than Π_0 is consistent with (20).

ideas.what: Torsion-free complement Π_0 of {±1} in Γ(2) (free on λ_0, λ_1, with λ_0λ_1λ_∞ = 1, normalised by sign changes), and its profinite stability under the GT-type automorphism group
ideas.modern_name: Splitting Γ(2) = F_2 × {±1}; GT action on SL2(Z)^ and on the profinite free group of M_{0,4}/M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical for the group theory; the GT action on SL2(Z)^ is due to Drinfeld/Ihara, with Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura (late 1980s–1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and SL2 only in outline

ideas.what: Normalisation of the conjugating elements α, β in u(ρ) = int(α)ρ, u(σ) = ε int(β)σ by requiring them to lie in the torsion-free complement
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of GT parameters (cf. f ∈ F_2^' in Drinfeld's GT)

ideas.what: Presentation of GL2(Z)/Π_0 (order 24) and SL2(Z)/Π_0 ≅ dicyclic group of order 12, a central extension of S_3 by ±1
ideas.modern_name: Binary dihedral group Dic_3 = SL2(Z)/Γ(2)-torsion-free part

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-theoretic bookkeeping: finite quotients of GL2(Z) modulo a free index-2 subgroup of Γ(2), and normalisation of cocycle data for GT-type automorphisms. This is standard and well covered in the later GT/SL2(Z)^ literature. The only noteworthy point is a sign/convention ambiguity, which Grothendieck himself revises on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Line (24): the crossed-out symbol before 𝔊 looks like a struck-through Π_0 or 𝔖. The intended intersection is probably with the orientation-preserving subgroup, not 𝔊.
Margin note next to (24)-(25): 'item en remplaçant 𝔊, Π par 𝔊^, Π^' — the hats are on 𝔊 and Π (profinite completions).
(25): the first entry reads 'Π_τ = μ_τ.Π' (an overwritten Π/μ), consistent with the second line.
'Les relations (20), ne déterminent α, β que "modulo μ"' — the quoted word is hard to read; 'modulo μ' or 'modulo signe' is plausible.
(29) margin: 'i.e. λ_1 = 1' is written at the right edge after the crossed-out 'τ(ρ)=ρ'; the last line reads '(et implique λ_∞ = λ_0 = 1 en conjuguant ρ)'.
